Generate a per-subject visit schedule with fixed spacing and jitter

Source: R/interval_censoring.R
visit_schedule.Rd

Builds the per-subject data-frame form of visits that add_interval_censoring accepts: assessments every every time units from 0 to end, optionally perturbed per subject by up to jitter (a common pattern in trial simulation – scheduled visits rarely land exactly on the nominal day). The baseline visit (time = 0) is never jittered, so the result always satisfies add_interval_censoring()'s "must start at 0" requirement.

Usage

visit_schedule(
  n,
  every,
  end,
  jitter = 0,
  jitter_dist = c("uniform", "normal"),
  jitter_trunc = 2,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

n

Integer. Number of subjects; schedules are generated for ID = 1:n (remap the ID column afterward if your events uses different subject identifiers).

every

Positive numeric scalar. Nominal spacing between visits.

end

Non-negative numeric scalar. Last nominal visit time (the schedule is seq(0, end, by = every) before jitter).

jitter

Non-negative numeric scalar (default 0, no jitter). Each non-baseline visit is perturbed by an independent draw from jitter_dist: jitter is the draw's half-width for "uniform" (stats::runif(1, -jitter, jitter)) or its standard deviation for "normal", which is truncated at +/- jitter_trunc * jitter (see jitter_trunc) and drawn via inverse-CDF (stats::qnorm() on a stats::runif() restricted to the truncated range) – one uniform draw per visit either way, so both distributions consume the seeded stream the same shape of way.

jitter_dist

"uniform" (default; unchanged behavior and seeds from before this argument existed) or "normal" (truncated, see jitter_trunc; its seeds changed when the truncation/bound was added – see NEWS.md).

jitter_trunc

Positive numeric scalar, default 2. Only used for jitter_dist = "normal": the truncation half-width, in standard deviations, of the truncated normal jitter draw. Ignored for "uniform".

seed

Optional integer. If supplied, set.seed(seed) is called before any jitter is drawn. Leave NULL when calling this from inside a larger already-seeded workflow (this is how sim_tte_ode's own visits = argument uses it when given a jitter spec, so one seed reproduces U, any between-subject draw, censoring, and the visit jitter together).

Value

A data frame with ID/time columns, one row per subject per visit – directly usable as add_interval_censoring's visits argument.

Details

jitter is validated against every before any draw is made: the maximum possible deviation (jitter for "uniform", jitter_trunc * jitter for "normal") must be less than every / 2, which guarantees – by construction, not by a post-hoc check – that jittered visits can never cross order or collide (adjacent nominal visits are every apart; two deviations each smaller than half of that cannot close the gap) or go negative (the first non-baseline visit is at least every / 2 above 0). A jitter violating this bound is an error, naming the bound, rather than a silently reordered or clamped schedule.

See also

add_interval_censoring, thin_visits and visit_schedule_informative, to layer missed visits/dropout on top of the schedule this function returns.
